name: Starfield Calibration
description: Recorded alongside the 2003 Twin Moons Planetarium Project, Starfield Calibration reimagines The Stardust Engine's classic catalog entirely through Cassidy O'Connell's proprietary zero-gravity audio engineering architecture: The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™.
subtitle: The 2003 Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™ Remix Anthology
sunoMasterPrompt: 1980s synth-pop, mid-tempo space-rock, driving 4/4 gated drum beat, shimmering analog synthesizers, melodic fretless bassline, crystal clear female vocals, lush spatial reverb, celestial atmosphere [can be male and female duet instead if Ryan and Cassidy are singing]
linerNotes: To understand the music of The Stardust Engine, there is a distinct difference between the genre the band pioneered and the actual sonic architecture they use to create it.

80s Cosmic Pop (The Genre) is the generic, widely recognized sub-genre coined by music journalists and fiercely adopted by the fans (The Ironheads). It broadly describes the band's signature atmospheric blend of driving arena rock, lush analog synthesizers, and deep-space lyricism.

The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™ (The In-Universe Trademark) refers strictly to the proprietary, highly specific audio engineering and synth-layering techniques developed exclusively by Cassidy O'Connell following the 1992 Friction Catastrophe and first perfected on "Moon 1 (Tidal Lock)". While originally engineered around Cassidy's solo crystal-clear female vocals, 2003's Starfield Calibration expanded the zero-gravity architecture to re-engineer the band's classic catalog—supporting both Cassidy's solo vocal profile and Ryan & Cassidy's sibling duets.

studioArchives.title: The Nomenclature: Genre vs. In-Universe Trademark
studioArchives.content: While "80s Cosmic Pop" describes the broader genre, "The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound" is an in-universe trademark registered by CEO Holly O'Connell through Engine Room Records, LLC (fictitious in-universe registration; not a real-world USPTO trademark) to legally protect Cassidy O'Connell's zero-gravity synth-layering and spatial reverb architecture from corporate imitators.

studioArchives.title: Archivist Note: The Suno Prompt Engineering Guide
studioArchives.content: Studio Master Prompt for Starfield Calibration (Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™ remixes): "1980s synth-pop, mid-tempo space-rock, driving 4/4 gated drum beat, shimmering analog synthesizers, melodic fretless bassline, crystal clear female vocals, lush spatial reverb, celestial atmosphere" (use "male and female duet" when Ryan and Cassidy sing together).
